name: Chives
imageAlt: Illustration of chives with thin green blades and round purple flowers
description: A tidy perennial with slender, hollow green leaves and a mild onion flavor. In late spring chives produce round purple pom-pom flowers that are edible and attract pollinators.
uses: Snipped over eggs, potatoes and soups
Mixed into cream cheese, sour cream dips and butters
Edible flowers for salads and vinegars
Finishing herb for fish and baked potatoes
Traditionally eaten to stimulate the appetite and help digestion
Used in folk cooking to add flavor while reducing the need for salt
Sulfur compounds in the allium family were used in folk medicine for colds
benefits: Good source of vitamin K, and also provides vitamin C, vitamin A and folate
Contains flavonoid antioxidants and sulfur compounds
Adds flavor with almost no calories
medicinal.caution: Chives are rich in vitamin K, so people on blood thinners such as warfarin should keep their intake steady. Chives and other alliums are toxic to cats and dogs, so keep them out of reach of pets.
